item.title: Leeds United head-wrecking crew stay the right side of crazy at Chelsea - Graham Smyth's Verdict
item.description: Leeds United head-wrecking crew stay the right side of crazy at Chelsea - Graham Smyth's Verdict It's good to be just the right side of crazy. More often than not Leeds United Football Club finds itself involved in mayhem. That is an apt word for so much of all that has happened to and around this club since its very inception in 1919. There's been good crazy and bad crazy, everything from the daft to the scarcely believable. Leeds United is a club that rarely needs a second invitation to lose the run of itself. Even under the calm managerial control of Daniel Farke and the sober ownership of 49ers Enterprises, minds have melted and chaos has briefly reigned at times. Take, for example, the last trip to Stamford Bridge, when Leeds lost 6-3. Scorelines like that rarely make sense. That was, in the words of Jayden Bogle, a 'crazy game' and something that he wanted to put right. And what better way to do that than a good old-fashioned historical head-wrecking. It all started with a bit of cat and mouse. Leeds almost played rope-a-dope in the opening stages, seeing relatively little of the football and absorbing pressure. Chelsea saw precious little of James Trafford's goal, because Leeds stayed so compact and patient, looking for opportunities to nip in. Farke's three centre-backs all chipped in with important interventions but almost all of the defending was kept to the edge of the area and further out. It wasn't until the 14th minute that the hosts mustered a shot, Morgan Rogers pulling the trigger from distance and missing the target. Chances to break out were few and far between, but when Leeds did get hold of the ball they moved it well. So well in fact that they created two good opportunities to open the scoring. James Justin's cross from the right was perfect for Dominic Calvert-Lewin and his header was so close to perfect - only the crossbar saved Chelsea. Quick, slick football unlocked space on the left and Noah Okafor's cross was headed downwards by Calvert-Lewin and Emiliano Martinez held on. Having worked so hard to break Chelsea's spell of territorial dominance, conceding an opener will have annoyed Farke. A second source of chagrin was the manner of the concession. One long ball, one lost aerial duel, a missed handball, one pass to the left and a shot seared inside Trafford's near post. The keeper appeared to be well positioned but was simply unable to get a hand on a thunderously-struck shot. Leeds responded to the goal not only with annoyance, but like it was a grievous personal slight. The response was pure manic aggression. The first goal came three minutes after Chelsea's. Calvert-Lewin gave Chelsea a hard time of it in the middle, Okafor joined in and took a pass from the no.9 and then did all the rest himself. item.title: Macau GP: Kean Nakamura-Berta takes win after Enzo Deligny crashes out
item.description: Motorsport photo Kean Nakamura-Berta claimed a comfortable Macau Grand Prix victory after forcing early leader Enzo Deligny into a mistake at Lisboa. It was a tricky first few corners for the drivers starting on the front row as second-placed Mattia Colnaghi struggled to get away, while polesitter Rashid Al Dhaheri was immediately under attack. Deligny braved it around the outside of the Mercedes junior at Mandarin to grab the lead, before Al Dhaheri then lost out to both Nakamura-Berta and Yuki Sano on the run to Lisboa. Williams junior Nakamura-Berta spent the next couple of laps putting Deligny under pressure before a brief safety car period was triggered when ninth-placed Reza Seewooruthun was tapped into the barriers out of Mandarin by last year's F4 World Cup winner Jules Roussel. Nakamura-Berta continued to remain about half a second behind Deligny upon the restart until he suddenly closed on lap 10 of 16. The SJM Theodore Racing driver was right on the tail of Deligny on the run to Lisboa and the leader left his braking as late as he dared but it was too late and he ploughed into the barriers. This gifted Nakamura-Berta a huge 3.5s lead, which enabled him to stroke it home to the flag to take the victory. The British-born Japanese, Slovak driver, who was third in this year's Formula Regional European Championship standings, made up for the disappointment of crashing out of the F4 World Cup last year. His large margin was aided by R-ace GP driver Al Dhaheri spending several laps bottled up behind Sano's TOM'S Formula Regional machine. The qualification race winner eventually found a way through around the outside of Mandarin on lap 12 but there was too much for him to do to close on Nakamura-Berta in the remaining three tours. Alex Ninovic Alex Ninovic Alex Ninovic made a similar move on Sano at Mandarin on the following lap to return to his starting spot of third on the grid. The 2025 GB3 champion then set about battling Al Dhaheri, blasting ahead on the run to Mandarin on the final lap to finish second, 2.456s behind the winner. Nakamura-Berta's team-mate James Egozi also passed Sano in the closing stages to seal fourth. Sano then lost out to fellow Japanese racer Taito Kato (ART Grand Prix) on the last lap but proceeded to plough into Kato at Lisboa as he attempted to retaliate, with the unsighted Matteo De Palo collecting them. This meant Alex Powell (Prema) and Ernesto Rivera (Van Amersfoort Racing) completed the top six, while Colnaghi was eventually classified 11th after his startline strife. item.title: 'Not the right time' - Fernandes pauses Man Utd contract talks
item.description: Bruno Fernandes has scored in each of his past two games for Manchester United [EPA] Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes says he has been offered a new contract by the club but feels it "is not the right time" for discussions about his future. The 32-year-old midfielder is out of contract at the end of the season , though the club have the option to trigger a 12-month extension until 2028. He was left out of the side under previous manager Michael Carrick but says he has no issues at the club and has chosen to stay at Old Trafford despite offers elsewhere in recent seasons. He told Sky Sports: "The club offered me a new contract, so I think that, from their side, shows that they want me to stay. "There's no negotiations ongoing, but I've seen people saying that 'he's asked for more money, he's asked for more years'. If I wanted more money, I wouldn't be here. "I had somewhere to go to get much more money than being at Manchester United. I could have been in a place that is much warmer than Manchester. "Two summers ago, three summers ago, last summer, I always had the chance to leave and I always chose to be here." United chief executive Omar Berrada recently spoke about Fernandes' contract situation, saying: "It's true that we're having conversations about his new contract, but I prefer to keep that private." Fernandes has scored 75 Premier League goals since signing from Sporting in 2020 and last season set a record for the most assists in a Premier League season. His form has tailed off this season in a poor start for the club as a whole. United are 19th in the Premier League table going into Mauricio Pochettino's first game in charge against rivals Liverpool on Sunday afternoon. "We spoke about the contract at the end of last season," Fernandes said. "We came in at the beginning of this season speaking about the contract, but about the context of the team and the club, I just put that to a side because I don't think it's the right moment, neither for me, nor for the club, to be talking about negotiations. "The most important thing now is that the club gets back to winning games." 'He will see what Man Utd are made of' - Pulis on Pochettino's first game No fallout with Carrick Fernandes was dropped for the Premier League defeat by Bournemouth last month after being critical of United's approach in their heavy defeat against Como in the Champions League. But Fernandes says he did not fall out with Carrick, who was sacked on 12 November. "The manager came to speak to me before the Bournemouth game, to say: 'Look, I'm not going to start you tomorrow. There's nothing to do with the words of Como, I know people will make it around that. I just want to tell you that we need to change something, I need to make a change, performances have not been great, so I just want you to know that there's nothing to do with that'," Fernandes said. item.title: How lessons from football history reveal the real reason behind Manchester City’s decline
item.description: The best part of five hours after the final whistle blew at the Etihad Stadium and about 150 miles north east, Noni Madueke scored an equaliser to ensure the day ended with the equation ultimately unchanged. Manchester City will still go to Arsenal on Sunday six points behind the reigning champions. They could reduce the gap to three, though the evidence of recent weeks is that it is likelier to stretch to nine. That would surely end City’s title challenge. The theory had been that it would take a potential punishment for their 114 guilty verdicts to do that and, while City are appealing, a sizeable sanction may be still to come. Perhaps that is fitting: the title could be decided on the pitch, rather than in the courts. The temptation is to attribute a slide of three defeats and a draw in four games to off-field matters. Enzo Maresca has denied that is a factor , and whatever his players say in the future, that is overly simplistic. Rather, there are similarities with another side who spiralled from a 100 percent start into a wretched run: Liverpool won their first five matches last season, and then lost four in a row, while City began with seven straight victories a year later. In each case, the initial results came with evidence of flaws which did not halt them: until, suddenly, they did. Neither looked solid defensively or always had the right balance in midfield even when winning . In City’s case, Maresca has lamented a lack of clean sheets, with none in their last nine matches in all competitions, with 26 goals already conceded in the campaign. A new manager does not seem to know his best back four. His habit of making half-time substitutions, with nine in the last nine matches, can show a decisiveness or an inability to find the right formula before then. Some of that is understandable, as Maresca gets used to a squad that was revamped in the summer. The Italian started by impressing with his tactical acumen. Three months into the campaign, however, his team look too susceptible to the counter-attack and offer too little control in midfield. Perhaps it is unfair to criticise Maresca for being too over-reliant on Erling Haaland for goals; it should be a broader concern that, beyond Haaland, Elliot Anderson, Iliman Ndiaye and Rayan Cherki , not too many others are enjoying a fine season personally. Maresca returned to the Etihad Stadium aware of pertinent precedents. He has raised the subject of Manchester United after Sir Alex Ferguson and Arsenal after Arsene Wenger . Neither David Moyes nor Unai Emery mounted a title challenge after replacing a legend. When City touched stratospheric heights under Guardiola, there was always the probability they would decline after him, regardless of the scale of their funding, the legitimacy of those funds or the identity of his successor. item.title: Fred Vasseur furious with latest "unprofessional" Ferrari clash: "It's the same speech as Mexico"
item.description: Motorsport photo Ferrari team boss Fred Vasseur says Charles Leclerc's contact with Lewis Hamilton in the Las Vegas Grand Prix was "unacceptable" and showed "lack of respect for the team", with the Formula 1 team set for fresh crisis talks just three weeks after their spat in Mexico. Vasseur had to hold talks with both Leclerc and Hamilton for their costly Mexico skirmish and will do so again after his two cars tangled on the streets of Las Vegas on lap 38, with Leclerc to blame for leaving his front wing dangling on the inside of Hamilton, sending the Briton into a spin. Leclerc received a 10-second penalty for the collision, while Hamilton dropped to 10th and eventually crossed the line in eighth. Leclerc was classified in 10th place after the penalty had been added to his race time. Coming so soon after Mexico, the thought of his drivers tangling again and the prospect of fresh talks to clear the air had worn thin on Vasseur. "Charles, I want to see you at the end of the race, before anything else," Vasseur said on the team radio during the cooldown lap. When asked what that discussion was like, Vasseur tellingly replied: "It was not a discussion. I spoke. "I think he apologised, he understood, but the result is there. You make a mistake, you say: 'My mistake, I'm sorry'. But you [still] made a mistake." Frederic Vasseur, Ferrari Frederic Vasseur, Ferrari He added: "It's unacceptable. It's a lack of respect for the team, for the sponsors, the same speech as after Mexico. I think we had a clear discussion in Sao Paulo. Today it wasn't professional. I think it's probably the escalation of tension." Following complaints from Hamilton, Ferrari had already been in touch with Leclerc about the aggressive way he was squeezing the Briton. Las Vegas' oval-like slipstreaming race required a degree of trust and teamwork for drivers to move through the pack of cars, as not racing each other was not an option either. The race became a painful reminder that trust between Leclerc and Hamilton is absent. "We passed the message to Charles during the race to think about the team when he was fighting in the right way, but you can't freeze the position on this kind of race, because you are in the slipstream," Vasseur explained. "If you slow down, the guy who is behind you is overtaking you. And all the other teams were able to overtake each other 20 times during the race. You can't imagine the frustration for me, but more important for all the guys at home." item.title: Verstappen wins extraordinary race as Ferraris collide
item.description: The Las Vegas Grand Prix featured 'yo-yo racing' throughout the field with regular overtaking [Reuters] Red Bull's Max Verstappen won an extraordinary Las Vegas Grand Prix that featured 34 lead changes in a non-stop battle at the front. The leading group of 10 cars were tied together for the vast majority of the race as the lead constantly changed hands between Verstappen and the Mercedes drivers George Russell and Kimi Antonelli. But Verstappen was the one constant, always seeming a step ahead of his rivals as he debated electrical energy deployment strategy with his team. And in the final laps Mercedes' challenge unravelled as first Russell made a mistake and crashed trying to pass Antonelli, and the Italian lost out to the two McLarens of Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri going into the final lap. The world champion dropped to fifth going on to the Strip on the last lap but was able to reclaim the place from Alpine's Pierre Gasly at the end of the long straight. And there was more drama at Ferrari as Charles Leclerc earned a 10-second penalty for tipping Lewis Hamilton into a spin. Earlier, Hamilton had been given a 10-second penalty of his own for passing Norris off the track in a fight for position that also involved Leclerc. It was a grand prix more reminiscent of American oval racing than Formula 1, and it depended on unique circumstances revolving around the Las Vegas circuit and energy-starved hybrid engines this year. But there was no questioning the showbiz value in the city that prides itself as the entertainment capital of the world. The key stories of an engrossing race were: Verstappen's remarkable intelligence and control in the lead in the most demanding of circumstances Another dip in a dreadful season for Russell More controversy at Ferrari, as both drivers earned 10-second penalties for driving infringements in battles involving the other Verstappen in control despite lead changes Challengers came and went but Max Verstappen was never without the lead for long in Las Vegas [Getty Images] "How many overtakes did I do?" Verstappen asked his engineer on the slowing down lap, as he reflected on a race the like of which F1 has not seen since the famous Monza slipstreaming battles of the 1960s and early 1970s. "Yeah, and not many of them on the straight," his new engineer Tom Hart said, summing up how Verstappen had secured the win against the Mercedes challenge. Lap after lap after lap, Verstappen, who started from pole, would lose the lead to Russell on the Strip only to reclaim it at the last corner, usually going around the outside. If that did not work, and Russell passed later in the lap, or led across the line, Verstappen developed a trademark move around the outside of Turn Three to get back in front. item.title: Zaire Franklin shares unbelievable details of broken leg as Packers await his return
item.description: Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images Green Bay Packers linebacker Zaire Franklin has revealed that he completed two more periods of practice despite suffering a broken leg in what he described as a ‘freak accident’. The defensive captain returned to the field for the first time since fracturing his shin during practice, with his absence leaving a gap in Green Bay’s linebacker unit. Franklin had missed four consecutive games after initially believing the collision was nothing more than a dead leg. However, an X-ray later confirmed the extent of the damage. Zaire Franklin reveals he practised on a broken leg after Green Bay Packers injury Speaking about the incident, Franklin explained how an unusual collision left him with a fracture that he initially struggled to believe. “Somebody just kind of kneed me in a weird way. I’m thinking it’s just dead leg. I actually finished practice. I practiced two more periods on a broken leg,” Franklin said, according to ESPN’s Rob Demovsky. The 30-year-old was stunned when the X-ray revealed the injury, admitting: “And then once I got the X-ray and it was broke, I was looking like, I almost couldn’t believe it. It just looked fake.” Franklin’s injury was particularly frustrating given his previous record of availability. He had missed only one game through injury during his first eight NFL seasons before sitting out four straight contests this season. “The only thing that was going through my mind was, ‘D***, I can’t practice tomorrow?’ It’s been a journey but I’m glad we were able to push through,” he added. “Thank God for keeping my head down and really been leaning on my family. I’m just glad to be back.” Franklin recorded 41 tackles, one forced fumble and one pass defensed in six starts before his injury. He was also named a season-long captain in his first year with Green Bay after holding the same responsibility with the Indianapolis Colts for six consecutive seasons. His return comes at a useful time for the Packers, who have already lost Edgerrin Cooper to a season-ending Achilles injury. Head coach Matt LaFleur expects Franklin to participate on a limited basis, leaving his availability for the Rams clash dependent on how he progresses through the week. item.title: The Daily Hilario: ¡Vamos Republic!
item.description: Nov 21, 2026; Sacramento, CA, USA; Sacramento Republic FC celebrates winning the USL Championship against the Louisville City FC at Sacramento's Heart Health Park. Mandatory Credit: Scott Marshall-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Turned out to be a fun day of sports yesterday … away from the clownshoes of Chelsea that is. The USL Championship game was held yesterday, to determine the winner of America’s second rate soccer league. The league follows the standard US format of a regular season then playoffs, and my local team made it to the final for the second time in their history — a long twelve years after the first time (feels just like yesterday). The fun part about the Championship game is that it’s not at a neutral site, so The Republic got to have home field advantage just like back in 2012. That advantage was sapped a bit by the awkward kick-off time (12pm EST; 9am local) and the freezing temperatures of an early NorCal winter, but an advantage was eventually had. The Republic took the lead and generally dominated the game from start to finish, but the visitors capitalized on a rare error from the captain to equalize and then continued to threaten occasionally on the counter. The only real question was whether they could be broken down. The answer was, no. Thankfully, the penalty shootout swung the home team’s way — Sacramento’s stalvart goalkeeper, Danny Vitiello making two saves and taking Man of the Match honors — and we got to celebrate a second championship for the city. Fireworks and trophy lift in the daytime? Gotta be USL! (Fun fact: the USL have grand plans to establish a new top division to rival MLS, with the added feature of proper promotion/relegation. That’s slated to start in 2028, should it happen. They only have a handful teams committed to it right now, so we’ll see. Sacramento tried to make MLS expansion happen for many years now, but this may be a more feasible route especially with the new soccer-specific stadium being built as we speak .) And the day was still only halfway over! The afternoon brought even more non-Chelsea-sport joy, with the University of Washington taking down the defending national champions, Indiana in a game of collegiate handegg. It’s been a disappointing season for the Huskies overall, with great summer expectations dashed by injuries, questionable coaching decisions, and inconsistent play (including from some of the biggest stars on the team), but this win does put a bit of shine on things as we head into Bowl season. And then, the nightcap was a rather fun F1 race in Las Vegas. With the championship already decided, everybody was out there just having some fun and passing each other left and right. Even Verstappen was enjoying himself. Talk amongst yourselves.

item.title: Paras Mhambrey set to join Punjab Kings as bowling coach
item.description: MUMBAI: Former India and Mumbai Indians bowling coach Paras Mhambrey is set to join Punjab Kings as their new bowling coach for IPL-2027, TOI has learnt. Punjab Kings had parted ways with their bowling coach James Hopes recently. Mhambrey will thus chalk out bowling strategies with PBKS head coach Ricky Ponting and skipper Shreyas Iyer. "Paras has signed a contract with Punjab Kings today," a source told TOI. Mhambrey will thus be the second man from MI to join Punjab Kings after Hardik Pandya, who came to the Chandigarh-based franchise through a high-profile trade. Mhambrey recently parted ways with MI after a long association with the franchise. Mhambrey, who was India's bowling coach from 2022 to 2024 under head coach Rahul Dravid, has had two stints with MI. He was initially with MI since the IPL’s inception in 2008, and then rejoined MI after completing his tenure with the Indian team following the 2024 T20 World Cup triumph. Mhambrey is currently in Dubai as bowling coach of MI Emirates in the ILT20. He had also coached the India Under-19 team in the 2020 U-19 World Cup in South Africa. During his nearly three-year stint with Team India, the 54-year-old ex-India pacer-turned coach was credited by many, especially ace pacer Mohammed Shami, who kept gesturing towards him from the field during matches, for the Indian bowlers’ brilliant show in the 2023 ODI World Cup in India, and the T20 World Cup in West Indies in June this year. The Mumbaikar is a product of the BCA-Mafatlal bowling scheme under England fast bowling great Frank Tyson in 1990. He then went on to possess a rich 21-year coaching experience in his CV, a period in which he coached multiple domestic teams, including Bengal, Baroda, Maharashtra and Vidarbha.

item.title: Sharks Locker Room: What’s “Mature” Hockey? Celebrini Loses His Voice
item.description: The San Jose Sharks…are in the playoffs? The Sharks are third in the Pacific, after a 4-3 win over the Seattle Kraken: Michael Misa , Nolan Allan, Macklin Celebrini , and Ivar Stenberg scored. Of course, take being in the playoffs as of now with a massive grain of salt. San Jose plays, once again, in the weakest division in hockey. Their .480 Points % is well behind the Utah Mammoth’s .563. The Central squad owns the final wild card berth in the West. Also, all the Pacific teams chasing them have games in hand: The Anaheim Ducks and Calgary Flames each have one, and the Kraken have five. But to their credit, the Sharks have grabbed nine points out of their last 12, turning around a season that looked like it was on the verge of spiraling out of control. Hasso here today, nice win for the owner — Sheng Peng (@Sheng_Peng) November 22, 2026 After the game, Ryan Warsofsky spoke on trusting his fourth line to close the game and his definition of “mature” hockey, Celebrini praised Dmitry Orlov ’s power play work, Misa shared what the San Jose Sharks took from a week of hard practices, and Orlov gave the praise back to his captain. A deeper game story with micro-stats from Stathletes and game action clips, Sharks Insight, will be published soon. Ryan Warsofsky Warsofsky, on Sharks always turning to Orlov on the power play, in the end: Just a calming influence. He understands what’s in front of him. He can make those reads, and he knows when to shoot it. Makes a nice play to Mack, but also makes a nice play shooting it to the net when we have two guys there. Warsofsky, on San Jose Sharks’ third period: I liked our third a lot. I thought it was a mature third. They couldn’t get the goalie pulled, but we were forechecking still. We weren’t on our heels. Warsofsky, on what “mature” hockey is: Making them come 200 feet, not giving them chances, not handing them chances. There’s a lot of different situations. There’s puck play through the neutral zone. There’s, you know you’re late in your shift and [don’t] try to make the extra play. That’s putting it behind their defense to make them turn. That’s just a simple brand of hockey. That’s winning hockey that every coach talks about and just having understanding of playing on the defensive side of things and you’ll get offense from that and you just got to believe in that. As a result of that, he has far more of a clue than your average pundit about Newcastle United, the good an the bad. The one-time player was once again on media duties at St James’ Park on Saturday night for the Newcastle United 2 Arsenal 2 match. Pat Nevin on BBC Radio Five Live, commenting on the first half moment when Bruno Guimaraes almost headed Arsenal into the lead: “That would have broken a few hearts around here, a great run from Bruno Guimaraes. A very deep header, he’s a deep-lying midfielder. These Newcastle fans have watched him so many times in black and white and that was a decent half-chance.” Pat Nevin after Eze gave Arsenal a 33rd minute lead: “You felt as though it was coming. The Newcastle midfielders pushed up further and the second they did so, they were shredded. That pass from Kai Havertz is an absolute delight, he’s such a special player. item.description: Motorsport photo Seven-time Formula 1 champion Lewis Hamilton believes he could have beaten Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli in their battle earlier in the season had he been given more support from Ferrari . The Briton was speaking after the Las Vegas Grand Prix, where he had another clash with his team-mate Charles Leclerc , which sent him into a spin. He recovered to finish seventh , while Leclerc was penalised and finished 10th. Asked about 1996 F1 champion Damon Hill's suggestion that Ferrari should make him its number one driver, Hamilton said he had never asked for that status, but felt he had needed it earlier in the year. "I've never asked to be number one. I genuinely haven't ever asked," Hamilton said. He pointed to a stage of the season when he was well clear of Leclerc and the nearest driver to challenge Antonelli for the title. "I was second for a long time in the year, and at that point I needed backing to make sure we beat Kimi. There were a few circumstances in the season where, with the support, we could have beaten Kimi," he said. After the 41-year-old claimed his first grand prix win with Ferrari in Barcelona in June, he was second in the drivers' standings , 41 points behind Antonelli and 40 points ahead of Leclerc. He was also second after Monaco, Belgium and Hungary. Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari, Charles Leclerc, Ferrari Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari, Charles Leclerc, Ferrari Antonelli went on to secure the championship at the Mexican Grand Prix, one week before Mercedes won the constructors' title, and now has 402 points to Hamilton's 267. "I don't know, but it's not something I want to get into," he said when asked where his relationship with his team-mate goes from here. "These are questions that people are asking. At the end of the day, I performed as hard as I could, and I've been giving everything I could to get those points today. "We were just constantly hit with challenges, and I just kept my head down." Earlier in the race, Hamilton had been handed a 10-second penalty for leaving the track and gaining an advantage over McLaren's Lando Norris . "10 seconds was insane and very, very harsh," he continued. "I was avoiding colliding with them, and they could have just told me to give the place back. A 10-second [penalty] is nuts. But I came back and I got back into the fight, and I could see Max up ahead and I was like, we're back in the fight. The network lost approximately 7 million subscribers in a year, according to Disney’s annual report, which puts ESPN and ESPN2 at 54 million pay-TV subscribers each, down from 61 million a year earlier. That is roughly half of the 100 million-plus ESPN had at its 2011 peak. Awful Announcing reported the latest figures Thursday, and they quickly got sports media personalities talking. Some were stunned by the size of the drop, while others questioned ESPN’s programming choices and whether its push into streaming can turn things around. The filing says ESPN’s subscription revenue depends on how many people access its channels through cable, satellite and other TV providers, as well as how many subscribe to its streaming services. ESPN also offers its own ESPN Select and ESPN Unlimited plans, while some of its content is available to Disney+ subscribers through a dedicated ESPN section. item.description: FBL-FRA-LIGUE1-NICE-PSG - AFP Ferran Torres netted a decisive late goal as Paris Saint-Germain edged OGC Nice 3-2 to claim a 12th consecutive victory across all competitions. Speaking after the match, the forward explained why banking three points immediately after the international break mattered more than a fluent performance. Torres clinches vital PSG win on Cote d'Azur Ferran Torres scored with five minutes of normal time remaining to seal a 3-2 victory for Paris Saint-Germain away to OGC Nice, stretching Luis Enrique's side to 12 straight wins in all competitions. The result ended Nice's unbeaten home record this season and opened a five-point cushion over second-placed Lille at the top of Ligue 1. Although Mohamed Amoura put Nice ahead in the eighth minute against the run of play, PSG turned the game around before half-time through Senny Mayulu and Desire Doue. Torres then delivered a deft finish from an Ousmane Dembele pass to give Paris breathing space before Ali Abdi pulled one back in stoppage time. Torres stresses priority of winning after break Despite Nice threatening on the counter-attack during a tense second half, PSG stayed patient until Torres applied the finishing touch. After the final whistle, Torres underlined that grinding out results right after an international break remains vital for dressing-room calm . "This was a very important win," Torres said. "It wasn't our best display, but ultimately, we were competitive and got the three points, and now, we'll focus on the Champions League. It's always important to win, especially after an international break, as it puts the team at ease. Ultimately, we got the three points, which is our priority." How PSG weathered the storm at Nice Nice took the lead with their first chance on a counter-attack through Amoura and stayed compact defensively for much of the opening half-hour. PSG finally broke through on the half-hour mark when Mayulu converted a penalty after Xavier Mandza handled inside the box, before Doue tapped in from Achraf Hakimi's pass less than a minute later. After the break, Joao Neves controlled midfield tempo and PSG pressed aggressively to limit Nice's threat on Matvey Safonov's goal. Hakimi missed a 61st-minute chance to extend the lead before Torres stepped up late on to make the difference. Champions League focus next for Paris With three hard-earned points secured in their first fixture back since a 1-0 win over Troyes two weeks earlier, Torres and his team-mates can now turn their attention to European action. Staying top of Ligue 1 by five points gives PSG a strong platform as they shift focus toward the Champions League.

With a dominant 34-6 rout of South Carolina on Saturday night, Kirby Smart and the Bulldogs punched their ticket to the title game for a record sixth consecutive season. item.description: David Raya injury update David Raya will undergo further tests after failing to finish Arsenal’s 2-2 draw at Newcastle, with the club yet to establish the extent of the goalkeeper’s injury. Photo by Stu Forster/Getty Images David Raya is set to undergo an MRI scan after being forced off with an apparent left-shoulder injury during Arsenal ’s 2-2 draw at Newcastle United . The goalkeeper went down after collecting a corner and coming together with William Osula who had been barging him all game to stop him releasing the ball quickly. Raya received treatment before eventually leaving the pitch holding his left arm. Kepa Arrizabalaga replaced him in the 70th minute. Speaking after the match, Mikel Arteta confirmed that Raya would be assessed, with an MRI expected on Sunday to establish the extent of the problem. “Unfortunately, he had to come off, which is never good news,” Arteta said. Photo by Stu Forster/Getty Images “He will get assessed now, and probably he will have an MRI tomorrow to see what it is exactly, because at the moment, I don’t know.” Arteta was also asked about the incident which led to Raya going off. “It was a knock. I don’t know how it happened and what the injury is at the moment, so we have to wait and see tomorrow.” Before going off at Newcastle, Raya had played every minute of Arsenal’s Premier League and Champions League matches this season and it’s hard to ignore the drop-off in quality between the Spaniard and his back-up. item.title: Georgia Makes SEC History After Blowout Win Against South Carolina
item.description: Georgia v South Carolina Getty The Georgia Bulldogs have made SEC history after beating the South Carolina Gamecocks 34-6 on Saturday night. Georgia finishes its SEC regular-season schedule at 8-1 (10-1 overall) and has clinched a spot in the SEC Championship. The Bulldogs are the first team in SEC history to reach the conference title game six consecutive seasons. In the last five SEC Championship appearances, Georgia has gone 3-2. The Bulldogs won the game in 2022, 2024, and 2025. Georgia lost to Alabama in the 2021 and 2023 championship games. Kirby Smart Is Not Focused on SEC Championship Right Now Shortly after beating South Carolina, Bulldogs head coach Kirby Smart spoke to ABC’s Laura Rutledge, and he was asked about clinching a spot in the SEC title game. Smart didn’t take the bait and kept his focus on the team’s next opponent. “I would say we’ve got Georgia Tech next week,” Smart said . “I am smart enough to know what that means. Go Dawgs.” Now the question is who Georgia will face in Atlanta on Dec. 5. Alabama, Tennessee, and Texas are tied for second place in the SEC standings entering Week 13, and things would get interesting if all three teams win next weekend. Georgia Can Win Its Seventh SEC Championship Game This year’s SEC Championship game is significant because it’s the final one. The College Football Playoff is expanding to 24 teams, which means league title games are going away. “Not a real comment,” Smart said earlier this month when asked about his reaction to the SEC Championship game going away, per Sara Tidwell of the Athens Banner-Herald. “I think we all kind of knew, right? It’s not really news that it’s breaking. It’s more kind of when they decide to go to 24. Sounds like the SEC Championship will go away, and I honestly don’t concern myself with that at all. I don’t have a lot of commentary about it. “I think it’s a great, historic game. It’s great for the players, the programs, the fans. The location has been awesome for us, and the venue is incredible. All those things are awesome, but times, they are changing and as they change, we’ve got to adapt with it.” Georgia has a chance to win its 17th SEC title. The Bulldogs currently have the second-most conference championships and are behind Alabama, which has 30. Georgia will be playing in its 14th SEC title game and has a chance to win it for the seventh time. item.title: Bayern Munich considering Jamal Musiala sale after health problems
item.description: Bayern Munich are considering selling Jamal Musiala over concerns that his ongoing health problems will prevent him from returning to his best form. Musiala, 23, was diagnosed with a “neurological dysfunction” after suffering an on-pitch collapse twice in a matter of days during pre-season friendlies against Heidenheim and RB Leipzig. The Germany international said he was “very optimistic... there is no additional health risk beyond this” and indicated the condition would not hamper his highly promising career. However, Bayern chief Karl-Heinz Rummenigge has now admitted that the club are assessing his future amid a downturn in performances, publicly questioning whether the club can now justify his lofty salary. Rummenigge told Sky Germany : “He has a health-related issue. It's also well known that he has a contract involving very substantial sums of money. As a club, we have to consider how to deal with that situation. I think that's responsible and perfectly normal. “What we know unfortunately suggests it will be difficult for him to get back to the level he has often shown here in this stadium.” Musiala was reportedly Bayern’s best-paid player until Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane penned a contract extension earlier this month. He has been limited to just four appearances in the Bundesliga this term due to a muscle injury, scoring one goal and notching one assist, with fitness problems continuing to plague him after spending over half of last season out with a broken leg. Rummenigge says “a decision will have to be made” over his future if he fails to show signs of improvement, but admitted that the former Chelsea academy product’s health issues would make a sale difficult. Rummenigge added: “We need to talk to the family, the player, and the agency, because then these sums of money, sorry, with all due respect, are no longer feasible. “I cannot imagine that Jamal wants to leave the club or that any other club would buy him under these conditions. “We are all interested in his return, ideally in top form. But what happens if that isn’t the case? Then we still have to think about the finances. “The discussion hasn’t taken place yet. These are just ideas at this stage.”

item.description: Lewis Hall Kai Havertz It was a game of varying fortunes for Lewis Hall against Arsenal. In a first half when Newcastle United struggled to even get out of their own half, the England left-back was one of the very few prepared to take responsibility and try to keep the ball, even when under pressure. When dealing with a difficult ball and facing his own goal just after the half hour mark, Lewis Hall attempted to get the ball down and keep possession. It backfired though with Kai Havertz stealing possession and played in Eze for the opening goal. Like the rest of the team, a far better second half from Lewis Hall. Especially as with Newcastle United pressing higher as a team AND doing it well, it allowed Hall to play a lot more in the opposition half and use his attacking skills on the ball to great effect. Just as an absorbing game had gone into the nine minutes of added time, Lewis Hall was left limping after he had blocked a cross and having tried to carry on, was then having to limp off a minute or so later and be replaced by Sven Botman. Following the match, Matthias Jaissle asked whether Lewis Hall was now an injury worry: “Hopefully it is only just a cramp that meant Lewis Hall had to come off. That is what we are hoping.” Lewis Hall, along with others, had put so much into this match, it could well have been cramp. I know when I played football (at a lowly level!), towards the end of the match that can easily happen, you are fatigued and then when you are stretching the blocking of a cross/pass can impact you painfully and set off a cramp. Here’s hoping. Matthias Jaissle also asked about his other England full-back. Tino Livarmento had only managed 33 Premier League minutes this season as once again impacted by injuries, in that second half though we were reminded just how good he can be, both in defence and attack. Winnipeg Jets forward Mark Scheifele has officially become the franchise’s all-time leading goal scorer, moving past Dale Hawerchuk with his 380th career goal during Saturday night’s matchup against the Vegas Golden Knights. The 33-year-old reached the milestone in the second period of Winnipeg’s 5-4 shootout loss at Canada Life Centre. Scheifele converted a pass from Kyle Connor at 14:36, finding the back of the net to tie the contest at 3-3. His achievement earned him a lengthy standing ovation from the 14,107 fans in attendance. CAREER GOAL NO. 380 IS A HISTORIC ONE FOR MARK SCHEIFELE 🙌 pic.twitter.com/fDXmP85p2I Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) — Sportsnet (@Sportsnet) November 22, 2026 Scheifele’s latest accomplishment adds to an already historic season. He has since extended those figures to 557 assists and 937 points, respectively, while also holding the franchise record for games played with 985 appearances. With 380 goals, 557 assists and 937 points, Scheifele now holds all three major offensive records in Jets history. He also joins an exclusive group of NHL players to lead their respective franchises in goals, assists and points, alongside Alexander Barkov and Alex Ovechkin among active players. Selected seventh overall in the 2011 NHL Draft as Winnipeg’s first pick following the franchise’s return to the city, Scheifele has spent his entire professional career with the Jets. item.description: Mandatory Credit: Justine Willard-Imagn Images The Boston Celtics suffered a frustrating 97-96 loss to the Sacramento Kings , wasting a strong defensive effort and a solid performance from Paul George . item.title: Bayern Munich CEO backtracks on statement suggesting a pay cut for Jamal Musiala
item.description: Over the last few days, Bayern Munich’s management has engaged in a public discussion about Jamal Musiala’s health and whether he will ever return to his previous level. Amid these discussions, CEO Jan-Christian Dreesen suggested that Musiala taking a potential pay cut may be on the cards . When a player re turns from injury—and here we’re talking exclusively about the injury, not the absence seizures—he needs time,” said Dreesen (as captured via @iMiaSanMia ). He continued: “I did not say that we need to revisit his contract; I just explained that Jamal was injured for two months and is now returning. I also already answered your earlier question about whether we or a nyone else had any knowledge of this [before the contract extension]. We had no knowledge of it, and I’ve answered that clearly. So there’s no need to discuss contracts. We have a contract in place until 2030. It’s absolutely clear, and therefore there is no discussion to be had about that.” This clarification from Dreesen gives the impression that Bayern are now struggling to do damage control after realizing the severity of their blunder by holding these discussions in public. item.title: What Brent Brennan, Mays Pese and Gio Richardson said after Arizona’s OT at Kansas State
item.description: MANHATTAN, KS - NOVEMBER 21: Wide receiver Giovanni Richardson #5 of the Arizona Wildcats runs into the end zone for a two point conversion against cornerback Nick McClellan #34 of the Kansas State Wildcats in the second half at Bill Snyder Family Football Stadium on November 21, 2026 in Manhattan, Kansas. (Photo by Peter Aiken/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Arizona football coaching staff knew there was a chance the Wildcats would get a rain game in Manhattan, Kansas. They also knew there was no way to adequately prepare for the tropical storm like conditions Arizona faced Saturday night practicing in Tucson’s 75-degree weather. “Full disclosure, there’s zero way to prepare for that, zero,” Arizona coach Brent Brennan said after his team’s 35-28 overtime win at Kansas State. Despite facing adverse weather conditions and a double-digit fourth quarter deficit, Arizona hung on for its eighth win of the season. “This was special, and winning at a place like this that is always hard to play at,” Brennan said. Our recap of the game can be found here , as can our game grades . Below is what Brennan, defensive lineman Mays Pese and wide receiver Gio Richardson had to say postgame. Brennan on the victory: “Well, first of all, hats off to Coach Klein and Kansas State. Those kids played their ass off tonight. It was a hell of a football game, so I just give them a lot of credit. I’m super proud of our team. They just kept believing, they kept fighting, they kept playing, battled through some incredible conditions that I think probably most of the kids on our team haven’t played in for a while, or even some of our staff hasn’t coached him for a while, but we finished the job and I think that what good teams do. [Noah] Fifita is an absolute warrior. He is without question the one of the best players in college football, and that should be not even hard to see. His ability to complete passes when he had to, in those circumstances is unreal, absolutely unreal. Winning doesn’t cover up the fact that we still have work to do. There were some missed opportunities there, some things that we can coach better, some things that we can fix. But I’m just incredibly proud of our team, just their belief, their fight, how they kept playing for each other, and we’ve got stuff to work on, but we’re going to celebrate the hell out of this. This was special, and winning at a place like this that is always hard to play at. You throw in the weather and the wind and the cold, and our kids just kept showing up for each other, and that is special. item.title: How Columbus Crew turned it all around to set up MLS playoff showdown vs. Messi
item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. But he wasn’t the right fit for the Crew in the post-Nancy era. The Crew turned to Courtois, a former Crew academy and MLS Next Pro coach who continued the idea first expressed on the field so successfully by Nancy’s teams. The squad might not have been the entirely right squad, either. item.title: Gotham FC’s title defense comes to crushing end in semifinal loss after venue change
item.description: They came by car, by the special-event X80 bus, by bike if they were feeling sporty. They came in layers, in beanies and scarves, with Gotham’s black-and-sky-blue colors on top. They came on behalf of those who couldn’t come, capacity being reduced at this impromptu change of venue, each one trying to make noise for five. Gotham FC forward Sam Kerr (20) competes for the ball against Kansas City Current defender Gabrielle Robinson (24) on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in New York City. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect They came with some measure of outrage — these home-field shenanigans would never happen in men’s sports — while their better angels told them to come in joy, in celebration, everyone watching women’s sports. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. But I would say it had no effect on performance today.” The match had been moved to Icahn on Monday due to concerns over the disintegrating field conditions at Sports Illustrated, which had unfortunately overshadowed Gotham’s quarterfinal victory there last weekend. Gotham was unbeaten in its past 13 matches at Sports Illustrated, which is operated by the Red Bulls of MLS. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month. item.title: On MLS Decision Day, D.C. United faces a familiar reality: Another season of failure
item.description: WASHINGTON — All around Major League Soccer , from Montreal to Miami and Seattle to San Diego, Saturday was Decision Day — the last act in an 8½-month production. While three playoff berths were in the balance, teams with guaranteed spots sought to improve their place. It's a day marked by desperation, scoreboard-watching and playoff-planning. At Audi Field, however, Decision Day felt more like Derision Day. For the seventh consecutive year, D.C. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses. Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer. United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier. The lowly finale was against another failed side, New York City FC, which claimed a 1-0 victory on a late goal. While 2026 was an anomaly for the New Yorkers, it was the norm in the nation's capital. D.C. added another sad chapter to a rotten story under an ownership group, led by Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan, that has dragged the organization into irrelevance in not just the prospering league but in the local market and the ascending sport. The public-address announcer introduces the team as "your four-time MLS Cup champions," but he's been saying that for a long time. Given the league's evolution, it feels even longer. United's last title, in 2004, came in a 10-team operation — one-third the current landscape. Since then, 13 different clubs have hoisted the trophy. Less than two miles north of Audi Field, the U.S. Capitol witnessed a historic sea change Tuesday with a political wave that swept the ruling party out of office. Local soccer fans have had no such luck with those in power at Audi Field. Under the current regime … United hasn't won a playoff game in 11 years and hasn't advanced to the conference finals in 14. Twelve years have passed since it won at least half its 34 matches. United's only trophy in recent memory was the 2013 U.S. Open Cup, which came amid a horrific, three-win regular season. D.C. is on its fourth head coach since Ben Olsen's departure in late 2020 and its second head of soccer operations in four years. The current director, Erkut Sogut — an agent best known for representing former German star Mesut Özil — was hired last fall without any experience working for a team. Another goal conceded, another season to forget. Keisuke Kurokawa's frustration summed up D.C. United's latest disappointing chapter. Scott Taetsch via Getty Images United remains one of three MLS organizations without a developmental team bridging the youth academy to the first team.
